title: Dream board
author: Priya N.
desc: Sort what you dream of from what you have to do and what you want to do, all on one page.

title: Dreamspace plan
author: Lilly Field
desc: The whole plan for one calm creative space, from the core loop to the vision, with what is shipped and what is next.

title: Idea map
author: Lilly Field
desc: Every part of the product on one map, tagged shipped, building, queued or idea, so you see what comes next.

title: Metro map
author: Lilly Field
desc: The same plan drawn like a transit map, with lines for the loop, the canvas, sharing and the gallery.

title: Our week, together
author: Tomás R.
desc: Everyone drops what they need, then the AI turns it into a fair plan for who takes what this week.

title: Plan a trip with friends
author: Amara O.
desc: Put dates, budgets and wishes side by side, see where you all overlap, and pick the place by Wednesday.

title: Party everyone pitches in on
author: Mara & Joe
desc: Lay out the party, let each person claim a job on a blue note, then get a countdown for the day.

title: Learn something in a month
author: Kenji Watanabe
desc: Pick one thing, split it into four small weeks, and shrink the plan with the AI when life gets in the way.

title: Save for something real
author: Fatima A.
desc: Name the thing you want, see where your money goes, and find the small changes that get you there by the date.

title: Side project, first weekend
author: Lars
desc: Turn an idea into a one line goal, a Saturday and Sunday plan, and a list of what to skip for now.

title: Drop, shrink or hand off
author: Chloé B.
desc: List your have-tos, then sort each one into drop, shrink or hand off, and ask the AI for an honest second look.

title: Make one chore smaller
author: Diego M.
desc: Take the chore you dread, say why it exists, and find a version that takes 15 minutes instead of 90.

title: Your first time with AI
author: Nomvula K.
desc: Say what you want in plain words, reply when it is not right, and try four easy first asks.

title: Say the hard thing kindly
author: Ruth E.
desc: Lay out what happened and what you want, then get a calm message you can read out loud before you send it.
